question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution'.
Satya is always great to his friends who helped him when he was in trouble.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. grateful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "grateful" means feeling or showing thanks; appreciative of a kindness received, and is the correct word to describe a person's attitude towards those who helped him.
◦ Example: I am grateful to you for your support during my illness.

• The sentence requires an adjective describing Satya's feeling towards friends who helped him, so "great" (meaning important/large) must be replaced with "grateful" (meaning thankful).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "greatful" is not a standard English word — it is a common misspelling that students mistakenly use for "grateful".

• Option 2: "thanked" is a verb (past tense), and cannot grammatically replace an adjective slot after the linking verb "is"; "Satya is always thanked" changes the meaning to Satya being thanked by others, not Satya feeling thankful.

• Option 3: "no substitution" is incorrect because "great" does not fit the intended meaning of the sentence at all; a substitution is clearly required.

NOTE

• Do not confuse "grateful" (thankful) with "greatful" (a non-word), "great" (large/important) and "gracious" (courteous, kind).

• Related word: "gratitude" (noun) — the feeling of being grateful.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Epitome
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Expansion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Epitome" means a summary or condensed abstract of a written work; also, a person or thing that is a perfect embodiment of a quality. (सार-संक्षेप/प्रतिरूप)
◦ Example: The report was an epitome of his three years of research.

• Since "epitome" (in its core sense of a condensed summary) means to reduce or abridge something, its antonym is "Expansion" — the act of making something larger or more detailed. (विस्तार)
◦ Example: The new edition is an expansion of the original short essay.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Exhort" (प्रोत्साहित करना): To strongly encourage or urge someone to do something; unrelated in meaning to "epitome".

• Option 3: "Lucid" (स्पष्ट): Clear and easy to understand; not an opposite of "epitome".

• Option 4: "Precise" (यथार्थ): Exact and accurate; again not an antonym of "epitome".

NOTE

• Synonyms of "Epitome": abstract, digest, summary, abridgment, embodiment.

• Commonly confused word: "Epithet" (a descriptive nickname/label) — different from "Epitome".

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
Mr. Surya / have no interior / motive in offering / you support.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. have no interior.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the sentence is "Mr. Surya", a third person singular subject, so the verb must also be singular: "has", not "have".

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement: A singular subject (he/she/it/a proper noun referring to one person) always takes a singular verb form (has/is/does/verb + s) in the Simple Present Tense.

• Correcting the error: "Mr. Surya has no ulterior motive in offering you support." (Note: the standard idiomatic phrase is "ulterior motive", meaning a hidden or secret purpose, not "interior motive".)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Mr. Surya" is correct as written — it is simply the subject noun phrase with no error.

• Option 2: "you support." is correct as written — it is the object of the sentence with no grammatical error.

• Option 3: "motive in offering" is grammatically correct as it stands within the sentence.

NOTE

• Common idiom: "ulterior motive" = a reason or purpose that is kept hidden.

• Other frequently tested subject-verb agreement errors on SSC exams: "he don't" (should be "doesn't"), "she have" (should be "has"), "the team are" (collective noun usually singular).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
The team always anticipate a bowling friendly pitch on their easy victory in the T20 matches.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. pitch for their easy victory.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The preposition "for" is used to show purpose or benefit — a pitch that is favourable for (i.e., in the interest of) the team's easy victory.

• Rule: When indicating that something is intended to benefit or favour a particular outcome, the preposition "for" is used (e.g., "a recipe for success", "a plan for victory").

• Applying the rule: "a bowling friendly pitch for their easy victory" correctly conveys that the pitch favours the team's chances of winning easily.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "pitch over their easy victory" is incorrect; "over" does not convey the sense of purpose/benefit required here.

• Option 3: "pitch to their easy victory" is incorrect; "to" does not idiomatically connect "pitch" with "victory" in this sense.

• Option 4: "pitch of their easy victory" is incorrect; "of" would wrongly suggest the pitch belongs to or is made of the victory.

NOTE

• Similar preposition usage: "a formula for success", "a key for/to victory", "an excuse for failure".

• Prepositions in English do not always follow a fixed logical rule — many combinations must simply be learnt as fixed collocations.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
The team will announce the winner tomorrow.
option_1: The team will announce tomorrow the winner.
option_2: The winner will announce tomorrow by the team.
option_3: The winner will be announced by the team tomorrow.
option_4: Tomorrow will be announced the winner by the team.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The winner will be announced by the team tomorrow.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "The team will announce the winner tomorrow" is an assertive sentence in the Simple Future Tense.

• Rule — Simple Future Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + will/shall + V1 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + will/shall + be + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "the winner" becomes the subject; the auxiliary "will be" is used; the verb "announce" becomes the past participle "announced"; "the team" becomes the agent with "by"; and the adverb "tomorrow" stays at the end.
◦ Passive: The winner will be announced by the team tomorrow.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because it retains the active structure ("The team will announce") — it has not been converted to passive voice at all.

• Option 2 is incorrect because the object "the winner" has not become the grammatical subject in a proper passive construction; "will announce" is left in the active form instead of "will be announced".

• Option 4 is incorrect because it wrongly begins with the adverb "Tomorrow" and drops the auxiliary correctly needed, producing an unnatural, ungrammatical passive.

NOTE

• Adverbs of time (tomorrow, yesterday, today) usually stay at the end of the sentence in both active and passive voice, unless placed for emphasis at the very beginning.

• Modal verbs (will, can, may, must, should) are retained as they are before "be + V3" when converting modal sentences to passive voice.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
By the end of / this month, he / will been working / for five years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. will been working.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence intends to use the Future Perfect Continuous Tense, but the auxiliary "have" has been wrongly omitted.

• Rule — Future Perfect Continuous Tense: Subject + will/shall + have been + V1+ing + (for/since + time).

• Correcting the error: "By the end of this month, he will have been working for five years."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "for five years" is correct as written — it correctly denotes the duration using "for".

• Option 3: "By the end of" is correct as written — it correctly introduces a future point in time.

• Option 4: "this month, he" is correct as written — there is no grammatical error in this segment.

NOTE

• Do not confuse Future Perfect (will have + V3 — action completed before a future time) with Future Perfect Continuous (will have been + V1+ing — action continuing up to a future time).

• "Since" is used with a fixed point of time (since 2019); "for" is used with a duration/period (for five years).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
Kamal is not willing to purchase a house on the 12th floor of a sea-side apartment, as she is fearful of heights. She is suffering from ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. acrophobia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Acrophobia" means an extreme or irrational fear of heights. (ऊंचाई का भय)
◦ Example: He refused to climb the tower because of his acrophobia.

• Since Kamal is unwilling to buy a house on the 12th floor because she is fearful of heights, the correct word describing her condition is "acrophobia".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "heliophobia" (सूर्य के प्रकाश का भय): An abnormal fear of sunlight.

• Option 2: "claustrophobia" (बंद स्थान का भय): An abnormal fear of confined or enclosed spaces.

• Option 3: "sociophobia" (सामाजिक भय): An abnormal fear of social situations or being judged by others.

NOTE

• Other commonly asked phobia words: Arachnophobia (fear of spiders), Aquaphobia (fear of water), Nyctophobia (fear of the dark), Xenophobia (fear/dislike of foreigners), Agoraphobia (fear of open/crowded spaces).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The homophone for the word 'there' is _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. their.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A homophone is a word that is pronounced the same as another word but has a different meaning and often a different spelling.

• "There" (indicating a place, e.g. "Put it there") and "their" (a possessive pronoun, e.g. "their house") are pronounced identically, making them homophones.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "that" is pronounced differently from "there" and is not its homophone.

• Option 3: "those" is pronounced differently from "there" and is not its homophone.

• Option 4: "clear" is unrelated in both meaning and pronunciation to "there".

NOTE

• "There", "their" and "they're" (contraction of "they are") form a commonly tested set of three homophones in SSC exams.

• Other frequently asked homophone pairs: to/too/two, write/right, whether/weather, hear/here, peace/piece.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Turned a deaf ear to
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Disregarded.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Turned a deaf ear to" means to deliberately ignore or refuse to listen to something, especially a request or complaint. (जानबूझकर अनसुना करना)
◦ Example: The manager turned a deaf ear to the employees' complaints.

• The idiom originates from the literal image of a person acting as if they cannot hear (deaf), in order to avoid responding.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "At intervals" (कुछ समय के अंतराल पर): Happening with breaks or pauses in between; unrelated to the idiom.

• Option 3: "By any means" (किसी भी तरह से): Using whatever method is necessary; unrelated in meaning.

• Option 4: "Rebuked" (डांटना): To criticize someone sharply; not the same as ignoring.

NOTE

• Related idioms of ignoring: "To turn a blind eye to" (to deliberately ignore wrongdoing), "To pay no heed to" (to ignore/not pay attention to).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
A bad patch
option_2: A period of time when a person faces lots of troubles
option_3: A person who takes a difficult path
option_4: A dangerous road to walk on
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. A period of time when a person faces lots of troubles.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "A bad patch" means a difficult period in one's life marked by problems or misfortune. (मुश्किलों भरा दौर)
◦ Example: After losing his job, he went through a bad patch, but things soon improved.

• The word "patch" here figuratively refers to a stretch or period of time, not a literal path or road.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "A path that is untravelled" wrongly takes "patch" literally as a physical path; this is not the idiomatic meaning.

• Option 3: "A person who takes a difficult path" incorrectly describes a person rather than a period of time.

• Option 4: "A dangerous road to walk on" again wrongly interprets "patch" as a literal road.

NOTE

• Related idioms: "To hit a rough patch" (to go through a difficult period), "A golden patch/period" (a very successful period).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.
An elephant is a large mammal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Tiny.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "large" means big in size. (बड़ा)

• Its antonym is "Tiny", meaning very small in size. (बहुत छोटा)
◦ Example: Unlike its large parents, the baby elephant was still tiny.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Bumper" (भरपूर): Unusually large in size or amount (e.g., a bumper crop); this is actually closer to a synonym of "large", not an antonym.

• Option 2: "Gigantic" (विशालकाय): Extremely large; again a synonym, not an antonym, of "large".

• Option 4: "Heroic" (वीरतापूर्ण): Showing great courage; unrelated to size.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "large": huge, immense, massive, enormous, vast.

• Other antonyms of "large": small, little, minute, petite, diminutive.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
Cannot be corrected
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Incorrigible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Incorrigible" means (of a person or their behaviour) not able to be corrected, improved or reformed. (असुधार्य / जिसमें सुधार न हो सके)
◦ Example: He remained an incorrigible liar despite repeated warnings.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Illegible" (अपठनीय): Not clear enough to be read; refers to handwriting/print, not correction.

• Option 3: "Incredible" (अविश्वसनीय): Impossible or hard to believe; unrelated to correction.

• Option 4: "Ineligible" (अयोग्य): Not qualified or entitled to do or receive something; unrelated to correction.

NOTE

• Commonly confused "in-" words: Illegible (unreadable) vs Eligible (qualified) vs Incorrigible (unreformable) vs Ineligible (unqualified) — students often mix these up on the exam due to their similar prefixes and spellings.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in bold to fill in the blank.
The modern work is deliberately ________ (ambiguous).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. certain.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word in bold, "ambiguous", means open to more than one interpretation; not clear or definite. (अस्पष्ट / द्विअर्थी)

• Its antonym is "certain", meaning clearly and definitely known, with no doubt. (निश्चित / स्पष्ट)
◦ Example: Unlike the ambiguous first draft, the final version of the policy was certain and unambiguous in its wording.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "puzzling" (उलझन में डालने वाला): Confusing or hard to understand — a synonym, not an antonym, of "ambiguous".

• Option 3: "dubious" (संदेहास्पद): Doubtful or uncertain — again a synonym, not an antonym, of "ambiguous".

• Option 4: "vague" (अस्पष्ट): Not clearly expressed — also a synonym, not an antonym, of "ambiguous".

NOTE

• Other antonyms of "ambiguous": clear, definite, explicit, precise, unequivocal.

• Related word: "ambiguity" (noun) — the quality of being open to more than one interpretation.

question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
A. Smoking in
B. Your youth stunts
C. The body and
D. Clouds the brain
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. ABCD.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Arranging the parts in the order A-B-C-D gives: "Smoking in your youth stunts the body and clouds the brain." — a complete, grammatically correct and meaningful sentence.

• Rule: In a jumbled-sentence question, the correct order must form a single sentence with a clear subject, a properly conjugated main verb, and a logical, meaningful sequence of ideas.

• Here, "Smoking in your youth" (A + B, forming the subject phrase) logically leads to the verb phrase "stunts the body and clouds the brain" (C + D), producing a coherent statement about the effects of smoking.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: CABD ("The body and Smoking in your youth stunts Clouds the brain") produces a jumbled, meaningless sequence.

• Option 3: DCBA ("Clouds the brain The body and your youth stunts Smoking in") is grammatically broken and without sense.

• Option 4: DBCA ("Clouds the brain your youth stunts The body and Smoking in") is likewise incoherent and grammatically incorrect.

NOTE

• In para/sentence jumbling questions, first identify the segment that most naturally functions as the subject of the sentence — it usually helps eliminate two of the four options quickly.

• Always read the fully reconstructed sentence aloud (mentally) to check that it makes complete, logical sense before finalizing the answer.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Barbarity
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Compassion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Barbarity" means savage cruelty; brutal or inhuman treatment. (क्रूरता / बर्बरता)

• Its antonym is "Compassion", meaning sympathetic concern for the suffering of others, leading to a desire to help. (करुणा / दया)
◦ Example: The soldiers treated the prisoners not with barbarity but with great compassion.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Callous" (निर्दयी): Showing an insensitive and cruel disregard for others — this is actually closer to a synonym of "barbarity", not an antonym.

• Option 2: "Compromise" (समझौता): A settlement of differences by mutual concession; unrelated to cruelty or kindness.

• Option 4: "Rivalry" (प्रतिद्वंद्विता): Competition between people; unrelated to the meaning of "barbarity".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "barbarity": brutality, savagery, cruelty, atrocity, ferocity.

• Other antonyms of "barbarity": kindness, humanity, gentleness, mercy.

question:
Select the word which means the same as the group of words given.
A written statement made under oath
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Affidavit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "Affidavit" is a written statement confirmed by oath or affirmation, used as evidence in court or before a legal authority. (हलफनामा)
◦ Example: He submitted an affidavit stating that all the documents were genuine.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Testimony" (गवाही): A formal statement or evidence given by a witness, typically spoken, not necessarily written or under oath in document form.

• Option 2: "Affirmation" (पुष्टि): A solemn declaration, sometimes used as an alternative to an oath, but the word itself does not mean "a written statement under oath" as a whole.

• Option 4: "Statement" (कथन): A general expression of something said or written, without the specific legal sense of being made under oath.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions often asked together: Testimony (spoken evidence by a witness), Deposition (sworn out-of-court testimony), Affidavit (written sworn statement).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in bold.
His mother never held a grudge against his father.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. benevolence.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The bold word "grudge" means a persistent feeling of ill will or resentment resulting from a past insult or injury. (मन में रखी हुई कड़वाहट / द्वेष)

• Its antonym is "benevolence", meaning the quality of being well-meaning, kind and generous towards others. (परोपकार / सद्भावना)
◦ Example: Instead of holding a grudge, she treated her rival with benevolence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "rancour" (कटुता): Bitterness or resentment — a synonym, not an antonym, of "grudge".

• Option 3: "revulsion" (घृणा): A sense of disgust or strong dislike; not an opposite of "grudge".

• Option 4: "malevolence" (द्वेषभाव): The wish to do evil to others — a synonym, not an antonym, of "grudge".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "grudge": resentment, spite, animosity, bitterness.

• Other antonyms of "grudge": goodwill, affection, kindness, forgiveness.

question:
In the following sentence, four words have been underlined, out of which one word is MISSPELT. Select the option with the MISSPELT word.
In spite of the dilemma that preveiled during the discussion sessions, the committee remained committed to finding an amicable solution to the issue.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. preveiled.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "prevailed" — the past tense of "prevail", meaning to exist widely, or to prove more powerful than opposing forces.

• Spelling key: PRE + VAIL + ED. The printed word "preveiled" wrongly swaps the letters to "e-i" instead of the correct "a-i" in "vail".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "amicable" is correctly spelt — meaning characterized by friendliness and absence of discord.

• Option 2: "committee" is correctly spelt — note the double "m", double "t" and double "e".

• Option 4: "dilemma" is correctly spelt — a situation requiring a choice between equally undesirable alternatives.

NOTE

• Commonly misspelt words related to this passage: prevail/prevailed (not "preveil/preveiled"), committee (double m, double t), amicable (not "amicible"), dilemma (double m).

• Remember: the word "vail" (as in avail, prevail, unveil) does not follow "ei" spelling.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
Don't let Dylan fool you!
option_1: Do not be fooled by Dylan.
option_2: Do not ever be fooled by Dylan.
option_3: Do not be fool by Dylan.
option_4: Do not have been fooled by Dylan.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Do not be fooled by Dylan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Don't let Dylan fool you!" is an imperative sentence with the causative structure "let + object + bare infinitive".

• Rule — Passive of Imperative (Negative, "let" causative) sentences: "Do not let + Object1 + V1 + Object2" is converted to passive as: "Do not let Object2 + be + V3 + by + Object1", which in common usage simplifies to "Do not be + V3 + by + Object1".

• Applying the rule: "you" (Object2) becomes the subject; "fool" (V1) becomes "be fooled"; and "Dylan" (Object1) becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: Do not be fooled by Dylan.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Do not ever be fooled by Dylan." wrongly inserts the extra word "ever", which is not present in or implied by the original sentence.

• Option 3: "Do not be fool by Dylan." is incorrect because the base verb "fool" is wrongly used instead of its past participle "fooled".

• Option 4: "Do not have been fooled by Dylan." is incorrect because it wrongly uses the perfect passive structure "have been fooled", which changes the tense/aspect and is grammatically inappropriate for a simple imperative.

NOTE

• Imperative sentences (commands/requests) are converted to passive using the pattern "Let + Object + be + V3" for positive commands, and "Do not let + Object + be + V3" for negative commands.

• Example: Active — "Post the letter." Passive — "Let the letter be posted."

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Atributes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Attributes" — meaning qualities or characteristics regarded as a natural or typical part of someone or something.

• Spelling key: AT + TRIBUTE + S, with a double "t" after "A". The word printed, "Atributes", incorrectly uses only a single "t".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Reinforcement" is correctly spelt — note "rein-" + "force" + "-ment".

• Option 2: "Opportunity" is correctly spelt — note the double "p" and single "t".

• Option 4: "Motivational" is correctly spelt — derived from "motivate" + "-ional".

NOTE

• Words with commonly dropped double letters in SSC spelling questions: Attribute (double t), Accommodation (double c, double m), Committee (double m, double t), Occurrence (double c, double r).

• Always check for doubled consonants in words derived from Latin roots — a very frequent SSC spelling trap.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Sleeping, dreaming and waking are three important (1)_________ for ordinary humans. But for those who have (2)_________ transcendental knowledge, all three are almost same and there is not much difference among these three. 'The world and life is a myth and it keeps on changing' (3)_________ Adi Shankaracharya, the greatest 'Advaita' preacher. Ramana Maharshi observed no difference between dreaming and waking states. What he said is that it is from one unreal world to another (4)_________ world. There is no difference between the images one sees when waking up and the images he/she sees during dreams. According to this great sage of the modern century, the first one is daydream and the second one is a night dream. The usual philosophers say that mind and body are the two elements and mind is the source of all diverse thoughts. In the waking up state, the mind is active with all tensions and dissatisfactions, so happiness is missing: during sleep as the mind is absent and so is the physical world, the real happiness (5)_________. It is said that deep sleep, where there is no feeling of body, mind and the world, is the natural state of human beings.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. aspects.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "aspects" means particular parts or features of a situation, idea, or experience, which correctly describes sleeping, dreaming and waking as three facets of human consciousness.

• The sentence structure "three important ________ for ordinary humans" requires a plural noun referring to distinct features/states, which "aspects" provides.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "problems" does not fit the context, since sleeping, dreaming and waking are being described as natural states/experiences, not difficulties.

• Option 3: "methods" is incorrect, as sleeping, dreaming and waking are not techniques or procedures.

• Option 4: "angles" is incorrect in this context; "angles" usually refers to points of view or literal geometric angles, not states of consciousness.

NOTE

• In cloze passages, always read the full sentence (and often the surrounding sentences) to judge which option fits both grammatically and contextually — the immediate collocation is often the deciding factor.

• "Aspect" collocates naturally with words like "important", "different", "key" when describing a feature of a broader subject.

In the waking up state, the mind is active with all tensions and dissatisfactions, so happiness is missing: during sleep as the mind is absent and so is the physical world, the real happiness (5)_________. It is said that deep sleep, where there is no feeling of body, mind and the world, is the natural state of human beings.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. deep.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adjective "deep" collocates naturally with "knowledge" to mean thorough, profound understanding, fitting the description of those with transcendental knowledge.

• The phrase "deep transcendental knowledge" correctly conveys a profound, advanced level of spiritual understanding possessed by enlightened persons like Adi Shankaracharya and Ramana Maharshi.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "large" does not idiomatically collocate with "knowledge" in the sense intended here; "large knowledge" is not natural English usage.

• Option 3: "superficial" is contextually opposite to the intended meaning, since transcendental knowledge, as described in the passage, is profound rather than shallow.

• Option 4: "depth" is a noun, not an adjective, and cannot grammatically modify the noun "knowledge" in this position.

NOTE

• Common collocations with "knowledge": deep knowledge, profound knowledge, vast knowledge, in-depth knowledge, thorough knowledge.

• Be careful to distinguish adjective forms (deep) from noun forms (depth) when filling a blank that requires modifying a noun.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank introduces a quotation attributed to Adi Shankaracharya, following the common written convention: "Quotation," says [person], used to attribute a general or timeless statement to its speaker.

• Rule: When attributing a quotation that expresses a general truth or a well-known saying, the Simple Present Tense ("says") is conventionally used, matching the present-tense narration used throughout the rest of the passage (e.g., "Ramana Maharshi observed", "What he said is").

NOTE
